pathway.title: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Deleveraging is real but earnings-led. AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. reports principal debt of USD 3,782.6 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 4,024.2 million at December 31, 2025, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA is USD 840.4 million against USD 387.5 million for FY2025. Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is therefore 4.50x, down from 10.39x, and 3.61x net of USD 751.9 million of cash. Most of the improvement comes from the earnings side, which means leverage will move back up quickly if earnings fall (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). The trailing figure combines FY2025 on the earlier Adjusted EBITDA definition with 2026 on the revised one, a difference worth about USD 0.9 million on the nine-month comparison and unquantified for FY2025.

Cash interest cover is adequate on trailing earnings but was below 1.0x a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.14x over the twelve months to September 30, 2026, against 0.95x in FY2025 and 0.86x in FY2024. A cover that moved from below to above 1.0x between FY2025 and the twelve months to September 30, 2026 shows how exposed debt service is to the earnings level.

Fixed charges beyond debt are the main cushion issue. Operating lease liabilities of USD 3,761.9 million sit outside reported debt, and cash paid for operating leases was USD 704.7 million in nine months 2026. Adjusted EBITDA plus rent covered cash interest plus rent about 1.35x on trailing figures against 0.99x in FY2025 (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). Rent does not flex with attendance, so the cushion falls quickly in a weak year.

Liquidity is cash, and cash is the only stated backstop. Cash was USD 751.9 million at September 30, 2026, up from USD 428.5 million at December 31, 2025, and no committed undrawn facility is described. Operating cash flow is seasonal: USD 128.5 million was used in the first quarter of 2026, then USD 235.4 million and USD 176.6 million were provided in the second and third. Free cash flow is USD 168.0 million over the trailing twelve months after USD 365.9 million of negative free cash flow in FY2025.

The October 2026 refinancing removes near-term maturities but adds debt. Pro forma principal after October 5, 2026 is USD 4,086.1 million, with USD 8.5 million a year of amortization before 2030, USD 2,816.0 million due in 2031 and USD 1,120.0 million of second lien term loans due in 2033; 79.2% is fixed rate. Pro forma total debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA is 4.86x. The fixed coupons on the new notes and second lien term loans alone are USD 303.5 million a year, and the floating margin on USD 850.0 million of first lien term loans is not printed, so pro forma interest cover cannot be computed from the sources.

Business risk is concentrated in supply and operating leverage. Seven distributors supplied about 83% of U.S. box office revenue in 2025, release windows have shortened, and attendance in the third quarter of 2026 rose from 58.4 million to 74.9 million on film popularity (Documentary Fact). The Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 9.4% to 20.3% on 31.6% higher revenue, the operating leverage that also works against creditors in a weak slate.

The record of dealing with lenders raises the monitoring bar. AMC moved 175 theatres and intellectual property into unrestricted subsidiaries in July 2024, financed there, exchanged USD 590.0 million of USD 950.0 million of the Existing 7.5% Notes into Muvico notes in 2025 with certain holders, and has repeatedly paid consent fees and exchanged debt in shares, lifting shares outstanding from 512,943,561 to 892,604,638 during 2026 (Documentary Fact; the creditor-adverse reading is Analyst Interpretation). It also repaid the Muvico and Odeon term loans in full in October 2026, which removes those structures from the debt stack.

runs.text: Strengths. Scale and footprint: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. operated 840 theatres and 9,472 screens at September 30, 2026 across the United States and Europe, with about 42.0 million loyalty member households, which gives it purchasing weight with studios and a recurring customer base (Documentary Fact; the market-leader claim is Management Language and is not adopted). Operating recovery: trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 840.4 million is more than double FY2025, and free cash flow turned positive at USD 168.0 million (Documentary Fact). Maturity profile: the October 2026 refinancing leaves only USD 8.5 million a year of principal before 2030 and pushes USD 2,816.0 million to 2031 (Documentary Fact). Access to capital: AMC raised USD 333.6 million of net equity proceeds in nine months 2026 and raised USD 3,970.0 million of new debt on one day, showing market access for now (Documentary Fact; the durability of that access is Analyst Interpretation). Cash: USD 751.9 million is held, USD 145.6 million of it by the International markets operations, whose availability to the group was not assessed (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. Film supply dependence: seven distributors supplied about 83% of U.S. box office revenue and windows have shortened, so revenue visibility is short (Documentary Fact). Thin fixed-charge cover: cover including rent is about 1.35x on trailing figures and was 0.99x in FY2025, and USD 3,761.9 million of operating lease liabilities sit outside debt (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). No described backstop liquidity: no committed undrawn facility is described, so a weak slate would draw directly on cash (Insufficient Information on whether one exists; the missing datapoint is the executed credit agreements). Higher debt: pro forma principal rises to USD 4,086.1 million, with USD 1,120.0 million of second lien debt behind USD 2,850.0 million of new first lien debt, so junior claims depend on collateral values the sources do not quantify (Documentary Fact; recovery is not assessed here). Creditor-behaviour record and dilution: the unrestricted subsidiary transfer, partial exchanges and share-paid fees show a willingness to restructure around existing lenders, and about 143,258,701 authorized shares remain unissued and unreserved, limiting further equity-funded exchanges (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Information limits: ownership, covenant levels and executed financing documents are not supplied (Insufficient Information).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The transaction that matters most for creditors is the October 5, 2026 refinancing, which closed after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is a subsequent event. S4 page:33 states that on that date "the Company completed a series of refinancing transactions", issuing 2,000.0 of 8.875% First Lien Notes due 2031 as issuer, borrowing 850.0 of first lien term loans under an amended and restated credit agreement, and borrowing 1,120.0 of second lien term loans from a lender identified as Deutsche Bank Special Situations Group (S4 page:34). The first lien term loans mature on October 5, 2031 with 0.25% quarterly amortization from March 31, 2027, and the second lien term loans mature on October 5, 2033 at a fixed 11.25% (S4 page:36). The 2031 Notes are secured on a first-priority basis, pari passu with the first lien term loans, by substantially all tangible and intangible assets of the company and the guarantors (S4 page:35). Intercreditor agreements separate three collateral groups: the AMC collateral, the Centertainment group and the Odeon group, and rank the Existing Exchangeable Notes first lien on the AMC collateral but second lien on the Centertainment collateral (S4 page:37). The proceeds repaid in full the Muvico Term Loans and the Odeon Term Loans, redeemed all 903.4 of the New 2029 Notes at 100.000% plus a make-whole premium of 144.3, accepted tenders for 355.5 of the 360.0 Existing 7.5% Notes and discharged the remainder for redemption on or about February 15, 2027 (S4 page:37-38). The company used about 32.7 of balance-sheet cash at closing and estimates a loss on extinguishment of about 182.7 in the fourth quarter of 2026 (S4 page:38). Taken from the CP-1 accepted figures, pro forma principal is 4,086.1 against 3,782.6 before, with 79.2% fixed rate, and the nearest large maturity moves from 2029 to 2031. The creditor mechanics are two: near-term refinancing risk falls, because the Muvico term loans, the Odeon term loans and the New 2029 Notes were the main 2029 and 2031 obligations; but senior secured claims are larger and a 1,120.0 second lien layer now sits behind 2,850.0 of new first lien debt, so recovery prospects for junior claims depend on collateral value that the sources do not quantify. This handoff states no expected recovery.

Earlier transactions explain why the structure is layered. On July 22, 2024 the company transferred the net assets of 175 theatres and 100% of certain intellectual property to Muvico through Centertainment, and Muvico licensed the intellectual property back to the operating subsidiary and engaged it under a management agreement to run the transferred theatres; Muvico and Centertainment (the Muvico Group) "are unrestricted subsidiaries under the indenture governing Holdings" for the purposes of the Existing 7.5% Notes (S1 page:100, S3 page:67). In the same month the company and Muvico jointly borrowed 2,024.3 of term loans and Muvico issued 414.4 of exchangeable notes to repurchase second lien notes (S1 page:156). In July 2025, under a transaction support agreement with "certain holders" of the Existing 7.5% Notes, Muvico issued 857.0 of New 2029 Notes for 590.0 of those notes plus 244.4 of new money (S1 page:95; S4 page:16), reducing the Existing 7.5% Notes from 950.0 at December 31, 2024 to 360.0 at December 31, 2025 (S1 page:142). The sources do not say whether every holder was offered the exchange. In 2026 the company paid consent fees in shares rather than cash, including 17,739,549 shares to holders of the New 2029 Notes for indenture amendments, exchanged all 155.8 of the New Exchangeable Notes for 142,102,295 shares with a loss on extinguishment of 33.0, refinanced the 400.0 Odeon Senior Secured Notes due 2027 with 425.0 of Odeon term loans that carried a Holdings guarantee, and raised equity (S4 page:14-18; S2 page:27). The 125.5 Senior Subordinated Notes due 2027 were redeemed on July 24, 2026 with proceeds of the June 2026 registered direct offering, within net equity issuance proceeds of 333.6 for nine months 2026 (S4 page:4, page:16, page:45). No dividends or shareholder distributions are printed in the nine-month cash flow statement (S4 page:4). Evidence quality for these transactions is High: they are filed, dated and issuer-specific, but executed indentures and credit agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity (what the documents permit) is inferred only from the filings' summaries.

fields.value: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. enters the cutoff with sharply better reported earnings, a refinanced and longer-dated but larger debt stack, and cash as its only stated source of liquidity. Adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 is 840.4, built from FY2025 (387.5), nine months of 2026 (707.2) less nine months of 2025 (254.3); against principal debt of 3,782.6 that is 4.50x, and 3.61x net of unrestricted cash of 751.9, down from 10.39x and 9.28x at FY2025. Cash interest paid over the same twelve months was 392.3, so Adjusted EBITDA covered it 2.14x, against 0.95x in FY2025. Free cash flow turned positive on the trailing basis at 168.0 after a deficit of 365.9 in FY2025. Most of the improvement comes from the earnings side: principal fell from 4,024.2 to 3,782.6 while Adjusted EBITDA rose from 387.5 to 840.4. These ratios are the clearest evidence of recovery and rest on filed statements, but they carry three qualifications. First, the trailing figure mixes the pre-2026 and the 2026 Adjusted EBITDA definitions (the effect on FY2025 is not supplied). Second, the 2026 operating cash flow is seasonal: the first quarter used 128.5, the second quarter provided 235.4 and the third 176.6. Third, no revolving or other committed undrawn facility is described anywhere in the sources, so liquidity is cash of 751.9 and no more; the working capital deficit excluding restricted cash was still 792.8. On October 5, 2026, after the quarter end, the company issued 2,000.0 of 8.875% first lien notes due 2031, borrowed 850.0 of first lien term loans due 2031 and 1,120.0 of 11.25% second lien term loans due 2033, and repaid or discharged the Muvico and Odeon term loans, the New 2029 Notes and the Existing 7.5% Notes. Pro forma principal is 4,086.1 (4.86x on trailing Adjusted EBITDA); before 2030 only 8.5 a year of first lien term loan amortization falls due, and 79.2% of principal is fixed rate. The stated coupons on the two new fixed-rate instruments alone come to 303.5 a year, and the floating margin on the first lien term loan is not printed, so pro forma interest cover cannot be computed from the sources. Operating lease liabilities of 3,761.9 and the 454.3 exhibitor services agreement liability sit outside the debt figure and are fixed claims on the same cash flow. Covenant headroom cannot be assessed: the filings give compliance statements but no covenant levels.

fields.value: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. is a listed, widely held theatre circuit with no sponsor identified in the supplied sources, and its creditor story is the interaction of an operating recovery with a history of active balance-sheet engineering. The operating base is large and geographically split: 855 theatres and 9,640 screens in 11 countries at December 31, 2025, and 840 theatres and 9,472 screens at September 30, 2026, with U.S. markets contributing 3,298.5 of 4,353.2 of nine-month 2026 revenue. Revenue is driven by attendance, which depends on a film slate controlled by a few studios, so revenue visibility is short and cash flow is seasonal. Against that, a largely fixed cost base (rent, operating expense and leases) gave strong operating leverage in 2026: third quarter revenue rose 31.6% and Adjusted EBITDA margin was 20.3% against 9.4%. The credit-relevant history is a sequence of transactions that moved debt and assets between entities: the July 2024 transfer of 175 theatres and intellectual property to unrestricted subsidiaries, the July 2025 exchange of part of the Existing 7.5% Notes into Muvico notes, repeated exchanges of debt for shares, and the October 5, 2026 refinancing that repaid the Muvico and Odeon term loans, the New 2029 Notes and most of the Existing 7.5% Notes with 2,000.0 of first lien notes, 850.0 of first lien term loans and 1,120.0 of second lien term loans. That refinancing is a subsequent event to the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is kept separate from period facts below. Supportive actions are also documented, namely large equity issuance and note-for-share exchanges, but they were dilutive: shares outstanding rose from 512,943,561 at December 31, 2025 to 892,604,638 at September 30, 2026. Ownership concentration, sponsor behaviour beyond the issuer's own actions, and executed covenant terms cannot be read from the sources and remain open.

fields.value: The transaction that matters most for creditors is the October 5, 2026 refinancing, which closed after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is a subsequent event. S4 page:33 states that on that date "the Company completed a series of refinancing transactions", issuing 2,000.0 of 8.875% First Lien Notes due 2031 as issuer, borrowing 850.0 of first lien term loans under an amended and restated credit agreement, and borrowing 1,120.0 of second lien term loans from a lender identified as Deutsche Bank Special Situations Group (S4 page:34). The first lien term loans mature on October 5, 2031 with 0.25% quarterly amortization from March 31, 2027, and the second lien term loans mature on October 5, 2033 at a fixed 11.25% (S4 page:36). The 2031 Notes are secured on a first-priority basis, pari passu with the first lien term loans, by substantially all tangible and intangible assets of the company and the guarantors (S4 page:35). Intercreditor agreements separate three collateral groups: the AMC collateral, the Centertainment group and the Odeon group, and rank the Existing Exchangeable Notes first lien on the AMC collateral but second lien on the Centertainment collateral (S4 page:37). The proceeds repaid in full the Muvico Term Loans and the Odeon Term Loans, redeemed all 903.4 of the New 2029 Notes at 100.000% plus a make-whole premium of 144.3, accepted tenders for 355.5 of the 360.0 Existing 7.5% Notes and discharged the remainder for redemption on or about February 15, 2027 (S4 page:37-38). The company used about 32.7 of balance-sheet cash at closing and estimates a loss on extinguishment of about 182.7 in the fourth quarter of 2026 (S4 page:38). Taken from the CP-1 accepted figures, pro forma principal is 4,086.1 against 3,782.6 before, with 79.2% fixed rate, and the nearest large maturity moves from 2029 to 2031. The creditor mechanics are two: near-term refinancing risk falls, because the Muvico term loans, the Odeon term loans and the New 2029 Notes were the main 2029 and 2031 obligations; but senior secured claims are larger and a 1,120.0 second lien layer now sits behind 2,850.0 of new first lien debt, so recovery prospects for junior claims depend on collateral value that the sources do not quantify. This handoff states no expected recovery.

fields.value: Earlier transactions explain why the structure is layered. On July 22, 2024 the company transferred the net assets of 175 theatres and 100% of certain intellectual property to Muvico through Centertainment, and Muvico licensed the intellectual property back to the operating subsidiary and engaged it under a management agreement to run the transferred theatres; Muvico and Centertainment (the Muvico Group) "are unrestricted subsidiaries under the indenture governing Holdings" for the purposes of the Existing 7.5% Notes (S1 page:100, S3 page:67). In the same month the company and Muvico jointly borrowed 2,024.3 of term loans and Muvico issued 414.4 of exchangeable notes to repurchase second lien notes (S1 page:156). In July 2025, under a transaction support agreement with "certain holders" of the Existing 7.5% Notes, Muvico issued 857.0 of New 2029 Notes for 590.0 of those notes plus 244.4 of new money (S1 page:95; S4 page:16), reducing the Existing 7.5% Notes from 950.0 at December 31, 2024 to 360.0 at December 31, 2025 (S1 page:142). The sources do not say whether every holder was offered the exchange. In 2026 the company paid consent fees in shares rather than cash, including 17,739,549 shares to holders of the New 2029 Notes for indenture amendments, exchanged all 155.8 of the New Exchangeable Notes for 142,102,295 shares with a loss on extinguishment of 33.0, refinanced the 400.0 Odeon Senior Secured Notes due 2027 with 425.0 of Odeon term loans that carried a Holdings guarantee, and raised equity (S4 page:14-18; S2 page:27). The 125.5 Senior Subordinated Notes due 2027 were redeemed on July 24, 2026 with proceeds of the June 2026 registered direct offering, within net equity issuance proceeds of 333.6 for nine months 2026 (S4 page:4, page:16, page:45). No dividends or shareholder distributions are printed in the nine-month cash flow statement (S4 page:4). Evidence quality for these transactions is High: they are filed, dated and issuer-specific, but executed indentures and credit agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity (what the documents permit) is inferred only from the filings' summaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. is a recovering but thinly cushioned credit: earnings have rebounded sharply, yet its fixed charges leave little margin if film attendance weakens. The strongest support is trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 840.4 million, which brings total debt to 4.50x, cash interest cover to 2.14x and free cash flow to USD 168.0 million, while cash of USD 751.9 million and the October 2026 refinancing push the main maturities to 2031 and 2033. The weakest point is that liquidity is cash alone, with no committed facility described, and fixed-charge cover including rent is only about 1.35x. What decides the outcome is whether attendance and the studio film slate hold near 2026 levels.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deleveraging is real but earnings-led. AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. reports principal debt of USD 3,782.6 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 4,024.2 million at December 31, 2025, while trailing Adjusted EBITDA is USD 840.4 million against USD 387.5 million for FY2025. Total debt to Adjusted EBITDA is therefore 4.50x, down from 10.39x, and 3.61x net of USD 751.9 million of cash. Most of the improvement comes from the earnings side, which means leverage will move back up quickly if earnings fall (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). The trailing figure combines FY2025 on the earlier Adjusted EBITDA definition with 2026 on the revised one, a difference worth about USD 0.9 million on the nine-month comparison and unquantified for FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover is adequate on trailing earnings but was below 1.0x a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 2.14x over the twelve months to September 30, 2026, against 0.95x in FY2025 and 0.86x in FY2024. A cover that moved from below to above 1.0x between FY2025 and the twelve months to September 30, 2026 shows how exposed debt service is to the earnings level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fixed charges beyond debt are the main cushion issue. Operating lease liabilities of USD 3,761.9 million sit outside reported debt, and cash paid for operating leases was USD 704.7 million in nine months 2026. Adjusted EBITDA plus rent covered cash interest plus rent about 1.35x on trailing figures against 0.99x in FY2025 (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). Rent does not flex with attendance, so the cushion falls quickly in a weak year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is cash, and cash is the only stated backstop. Cash was USD 751.9 million at September 30, 2026, up from USD 428.5 million at December 31, 2025, and no committed undrawn facility is described. Operating cash flow is seasonal: USD 128.5 million was used in the first quarter of 2026, then USD 235.4 million and USD 176.6 million were provided in the second and third. Free cash flow is USD 168.0 million over the trailing twelve months after USD 365.9 million of negative free cash flow in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The October 2026 refinancing removes near-term maturities but adds debt. Pro forma principal after October 5, 2026 is USD 4,086.1 million, with USD 8.5 million a year of amortization before 2030, USD 2,816.0 million due in 2031 and USD 1,120.0 million of second lien term loans due in 2033; 79.2% is fixed rate. Pro forma total debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA is 4.86x. The fixed coupons on the new notes and second lien term loans alone are USD 303.5 million a year, and the floating margin on USD 850.0 million of first lien term loans is not printed, so pro forma interest cover cannot be computed from the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is concentrated in supply and operating leverage. Seven distributors supplied about 83% of U.S. box office revenue in 2025, release windows have shortened, and attendance in the third quarter of 2026 rose from 58.4 million to 74.9 million on film popularity (Documentary Fact). The Adjusted EBITDA margin rose from 9.4% to 20.3% on 31.6% higher revenue, the operating leverage that also works against creditors in a weak slate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The record of dealing with lenders raises the monitoring bar. AMC moved 175 theatres and intellectual property into unrestricted subsidiaries in July 2024, financed there, exchanged USD 590.0 million of USD 950.0 million of the Existing 7.5% Notes into Muvico notes in 2025 with certain holders, and has repeatedly paid consent fees and exchanged debt in shares, lifting shares outstanding from 512,943,561 to 892,604,638 during 2026 (Documentary Fact; the creditor-adverse reading is Analyst Interpretation). It also repaid the Muvico and Odeon term loans in full in October 2026, which removes those structures from the debt stack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Scale and footprint: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC. operated 840 theatres and 9,472 screens at September 30, 2026 across the United States and Europe, with about 42.0 million loyalty member households, which gives it purchasing weight with studios and a recurring customer base (Documentary Fact; the market-leader claim is Management Language and is not adopted). Operating recovery: trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 840.4 million is more than double FY2025, and free cash flow turned positive at USD 168.0 million (Documentary Fact). Maturity profile: the October 2026 refinancing leaves only USD 8.5 million a year of principal before 2030 and pushes USD 2,816.0 million to 2031 (Documentary Fact). Access to capital: AMC raised USD 333.6 million of net equity proceeds in nine months 2026 and raised USD 3,970.0 million of new debt on one day, showing market access for now (Documentary Fact; the durability of that access is Analyst Interpretation). Cash: USD 751.9 million is held, USD 145.6 million of it by the International markets operations, whose availability to the group was not assessed (Documentary Fact).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Film supply dependence: seven distributors supplied about 83% of U.S. box office revenue and windows have shortened, so revenue visibility is short (Documentary Fact). Thin fixed-charge cover: cover including rent is about 1.35x on trailing figures and was 0.99x in FY2025, and USD 3,761.9 million of operating lease liabilities sit outside debt (Analyst Interpretation from the financial base). No described backstop liquidity: no committed undrawn facility is described, so a weak slate would draw directly on cash (Insufficient Information on whether one exists; the missing datapoint is the executed credit agreements). Higher debt: pro forma principal rises to USD 4,086.1 million, with USD 1,120.0 million of second lien debt behind USD 2,850.0 million of new first lien debt, so junior claims depend on collateral values the sources do not quantify (Documentary Fact; recovery is not assessed here). Creditor-behaviour record and dilution: the unrestricted subsidiary transfer, partial exchanges and share-paid fees show a willingness to restructure around existing lenders, and about 143,258,701 authorized shares remain unissued and unreserved, limiting further equity-funded exchanges (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation). Information limits: ownership, covenant levels and executed financing documents are not supplied (Insufficient Information).
